finding.claim: Medium, medium confidence. clamp_body_mode_to_ceiling lets a runtime BodyMode::Stream downgrade bypass a baseline SizeLimit, so request bodies are forwarded with no size cap. The code comment says SizeLimit 'remains the backstop', but SizeLimit is enforced only while ctx.request_body_mode is SizeLimit, and the same field is what gets downgraded.
finding.source: A filter in the configured chain that calls set_request_body_mode(Stream) on a condition the attacker can satisfy (for example, a path or header match). Precondition: a SizeLimit baseline is configured for the request body and some filter can select Stream at request-header time. Which built-in filters do this is in praxis_filter, which is not in this repo, so it is unverified.
finding.sink: Unbounded upstream forwarding in request_body_filter.rs (Stream arm is a no-op). The configured body-size cap is not applied.

trace.note: build_filter_context and execute_http_request run the header-phase filters, which may set request_body_mode
clamp_body_mode_to_ceiling: baseline SizeLimit yields ceiling Some(limit)
(m, None | Some(_)) => m: Stream passes through unchanged even when a ceiling exists
BodyMode::StreamBuffer{..} | BodyMode::Stream => {} : no size check; the SizeLimit check at lines 64-73 is skipped

finding.guards_checked: Clamp at mod.rs:183-199 and its comment at 176-182. The passthrough is locked in by test clamp_body_mode_to_ceiling_stream_passes_through_with_ceiling (request_filter/mod.rs:742-753). check_body_size_limit is called only at request_body_filter.rs:65 and response_body_filter.rs:52, so no other size check exists in the repo. Pre-read (request_filter/mod.rs:113-131) enforces a 413 for StreamBuffer baselines before header filters run, so this bypass is specific to SizeLimit baselines. The response-side clamp (response_filter.rs:115) has the same shape, but the response body is backend-controlled, so its impact is lower.

finding.claim: Plausible, low-to-medium confidence (unverified). The proxy does not reject requests that carry both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length. It strips Transfer-Encoding before forwarding and keeps Content-Length, which can produce a CL/TE request-smuggling desync at the backend. Whether this is exploitable depends on Pingora's downstream request parser, which is not in this repo or the local cargo registry.
finding.source: Remote client sending a single request with both 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' and 'Content-Length: N' that disagree in length.
finding.sink: Upstream request framing: upstream_request::strip_hop_by_hop removes transfer-encoding but leaves content-length, so the backend frames the body by CL while the proxy forwards the decoded body bytes.

trace.note: normalize_request_headers: runs reject_conflicting_single_value_headers and handle_obs_fold only
reject_conflicting_single_value_headers covers only Content-Length and Content-Type duplicates; no TE/CL check
strip_hop_by_hop removes the TE header from the upstream request and does not touch Content-Length
same sequence in the no-body handler

finding.guards_checked: Host validation (validation.rs:30-44), duplicate-CL/CT rejection (normalize.rs:75-99), obs-fold rejection on Host/Content-Length (normalize.rs:35, 141-149), and reserved-header rejection (request_filter/mod.rs:535-552). None of them rejects TE together with CL. The protocol-level behaviour of Pingora's parser was not verified because its source is not available here.

finding.claim: Conditional, medium-to-high severity. The admin listener serves unauthenticated KV write and delete (PUT/DELETE /api/kv/...) alongside health and metrics, on whatever address the operator passes to add_admin_endpoints_to_pingora_server. If that address is reachable from untrusted networks, anyone can change runtime KV state that filters may use for decisions. The default admin bind address is in praxis_core and was not checked.
finding.source: Any network client that can reach the admin socket. Precondition: admin_addr is not loopback-only or firewalled.
finding.sink: KV store mutation (set/delete) in kv/mod.rs, which is consumed by the filter pipeline.

trace.note: add_admin_endpoints_to_pingora_server: service.add_tcp(admin_addr), using the caller-supplied address
dispatch_kv_request: no auth check before routing
KvRoute::Set reads the body (capped at 1 MiB, line 25/129) and calls handle_set
handle_delete calls backend.delete(key) with no authorization

finding.guards_checked: Body size cap of 1 MiB (kv/mod.rs:25, 129). Route parsing rejects unknown shapes (kv/mod.rs:92-107). JSON output escaping is correct (health/service.rs:36 and tests). No authentication or authorization is applied to any admin route in this repo.
